label: first occurrence of b/s/z/k/j early in the original phase (t=1-4), boosted when the sequence starts with h/c/x/2/0/w/d/o/e
explanation: 98% of activation mass falls in the original phase, peaking at t=2 (54% of mass), then t=3 (28%) and t=1 (10%). It never fires at t=0 or on the delimiter, and only weakly in the copy phase. The input token matters most: b alone carries 42% of mass (rate 11%), then s, z, k, j (and more weakly p, a). It fires mostly on the first occurrence of the token (97% of mass). Whether it fires also depends on the earlier prefix: it is stronger when the first or preceding tokens are h, c, x, 2, w, e or 0, and the top examples are b at t=3 after prefixes like x h c or h c w. Restricting to b/s/z/k/j at t=1-4 covers 84% of mass, but precision is only 16%. Adding the first-token condition gives dev F1 0.42 (P 0.35, R 0.50, mass 0.64). The firing rule looks like a graded mix of the current token and the prefix, which a simple predicate cannot capture.
